format.description: The version of this file format. Always 1.

id.description: A name for this level, like "level-1". It matches the file name.

tileset.description: The tileset whose letters the rows use, by the id in its file, like "meadow". Left out means # is solid and . is empty.

backdrop.description: The backdrop behind the level, by the id in its file, like "valley". Left out means only the sky.

sky.description: The colour behind the level, which also fills the bars beside it, as # and six digits, like #9fd3f0. Left out means that light blue.

ground.description: The colour of the solid tiles, as # and six digits, like #3b4a5a. Left out means that slate.

w.description: How wide a part of the level the screen shows while the players are close together, in tiles.

h.description: How tall a part of the level the screen shows while the players are close together, in tiles.

w.description: The widest the camera pulls back to as the players spread, in tiles.

h.description: The tallest the camera pulls back to as the players spread, in tiles.

most.description: The most of the level the camera pulls back to as the players spread. Left out means the whole level.

view.description: How much of the level the screen shows, which switches the camera on: it follows the players and pulls back as they spread. Left out means the whole level is always in view.

tiles.description: The map, one text row per line, top to bottom. # is solid ground and . is empty air. With a tileset, each letter is one of its tiles.

id.description: A name for this thing, used once in this level, like "crate-1".

character.description: Which character this thing is, by the id in its character file, like "crate".

x.description: Where the middle of the thing is, in tiles from the left edge.

y.description: Where the middle of the thing is, in tiles from the top edge.

things.description: The things standing in the level, like crates. Can be empty.

x.description: Where the hero starts, in tiles from the left edge.

y.description: Where the hero starts, in tiles from the top edge.

starts.description: Where each player begins. At least one is needed.

id.description: A name for this joint, used once in this level, like "seesaw".

thing.description: Which thing is held, by its id in this level, like "plank-1".

holder.description: The thing that holds it, by its id in this level. Left out means the level itself holds it.

kind.description: "pin": the thing turns about one point, as a seesaw does.

x.description: Where the pin is, in tiles from the left edge.

y.description: Where the pin is, in tiles from the top edge.

min.description: The furthest it may turn one way, in degrees: 0 or less.

max.description: The furthest it may turn the other way, in degrees: 0 or more.

turn.description: How far the thing may turn from how it was placed. Left out means it turns freely.

id.description: A name for this joint, used once in this level, like "seesaw".

thing.description: Which thing is held, by its id in this level, like "plank-1".

holder.description: The thing that holds it, by its id in this level. Left out means the level itself holds it.

kind.description: "rope": the thing can go no further than the rope reaches, as a swing does.

x.description: Where the rope is tied to the thing, in tiles from the left edge.

y.description: Where the rope is tied to the thing, in tiles from the top edge.

x.description: Where the other end is tied, to the holder or to the level, in tiles from the left edge.

y.description: Where the other end is tied, to the holder or to the level, in tiles from the top edge.

slack.description: How much longer the rope is than the gap between its ends, in tiles. Left out means none.

joints.description: Pins and ropes that hold things: a seesaw turning on its pin, a swing hung from ropes. Left out means nothing is held.
